# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b11 — Area hubs and per-device climate controllers

**Opt-in beta 11 for Home Assistant 2026.10+.** This release combines the Area-hub hierarchy with the complete pending per-device climate, control-method, on/off PID and quiet-operation software. Stable **v0.5.1**, previous beta tags, the existing `air_quality_advisor` domain and original Home/Area entity identities remain unchanged. Back up your Home Assistant configuration before installing.

## Home → Area hub → managed equipment

Every configured monitoring, climate-only or PID-only area has its own logical hub. Room overview, calculated environmental values and area settings belong to that hub. Managed equipment controller devices are children of their Area hub. Physical devices stay with their native integration and gateway; Manager never replaces their physical identifiers or user area assignments. Multiple independently controlled channels on one physical device have separate climate entities on the same logical child.

## A real climate interface for each supported controller

Each managed endpoint exposes room temperature/humidity where valid sources exist, its actual supported HVAC modes, native fan and swing controls where advertised, and Manager presets: **None, Home, Comfort, Away, Sleep and Eco**. A fan does not acquire imaginary heating/cooling, and a dehumidifier does not acquire a fake temperature service. Binary heating/cooling equipment can use a Manager temperature target with an external sensor without calling an unsupported native setpoint service.

Presets affect the Manager targets; None allows automatic/PID controllers to follow room presence and sleep policy. Manual with None keeps independent user targets rather than silently changing them with occupancy. Fan selections can be saved per preset. The climate entity reports observed physical state separately from requested mode, profile, controller diagnostics and commissioning status.

## Per-device control method

- **Existing** preserves the previous room controller and is the upgrade default. No new equipment power permission is granted automatically.
- **Automatic** follows the room/preset policy using only independently commissioned device capabilities and valid measurements.
- **Manual** follows explicit user mode, target and native option choices, while retaining physical interlocks and dwell limits.
- **Off** stops this Manager control path and requests its owned equipment OFF after the original minimum run time. It does not adopt or shut down unrelated manually running equipment.
- **PID** appears only for supported feedback/control combinations. It supports thermal, humidity and qualified fan air-quality feedback. Kp/Ki/Kd, sample interval and cycle duration are editable per controller.

Existing room drivers yield the exact claimed endpoint, with live checks preventing two controllers from commanding the same device. Unrelated room equipment keeps its existing controller. A manual physical adjustment latches a pause rather than starting an automation fight.

## PID for on/off equipment

Commissioned fans, dedicated humidifiers/dehumidifiers and supported native climate ON/OFF modes can use **slow, time-proportioned duty control**. Direct qualified relay/percentage outputs are supported too. Integral anti-windup, bounded samples, pulse-length checks, minimum ON/OFF times and maximum continuous runtime are enforced. Short pulses that cannot meet the minimum runtime are skipped. Native setpoint-only PID remains bounded and cannot gain power-switching permission from a dropdown.

Compressor-affecting equipment uses a minimum ten-minute software ON/OFF floor, or the larger configured equipment minimum. These values do not replace manufacturer-specific requirements, independent electrical/thermal protection, frost/defrost logic or physical commissioning. Automatic power ownership will not take over an already-running manual appliance: turn the physical endpoint OFF and verify its safeguards first.

## Quiet during sleep or occupancy

Devices with a genuinely adjustable fan gain **Quiet during sleep** and **Quiet while occupied** switches. Percentage fans expose a quiet-speed limit; discrete fan controls expose their actual native choices. The controller lowers and restores the previous speed only when the current context is known and the fan remains under its ownership. It never starts an appliance merely to apply quiet mode, invents no unsupported quiet preset and makes no claim to measure or guarantee acoustic decibels.

## Recovery, localization and validation

Every physical command records a durable intent before dispatch and then waits for acknowledgement. It rechecks current identity, settings, source values, room interlocks and competing ownership immediately before the service call. Uncertain commands are not blindly retried. Restart/manual-override pauses require the device's **Reconcile and resume** button after verifying actual equipment state. Deselected or removed owned equipment retains its original timing for bounded retirement; changed physical identities are not commanded.

All 38 supplied locale catalogs include the new controller labels and help, including Greek. Python 3.13/3.14 regression tests, deterministic translations, frontend checks, HACS and Hassfest must pass before publication. These tests use simulated Home Assistant boundaries; **no live HVAC, compressor, fan or humidity device is certified by software CI**.

## Install and activate deliberately

In HACS select **Redownload → Show beta versions → v0.6.0b11**, then restart Home Assistant. Keep the existing integration entry. Open the Area hub and its controller child, complete the existing hardware/source commissioning where necessary, and change Control method from Existing only for the equipment you intend to transfer. Review the controller's help/status attributes and verify physical response before unattended operation.

The attached ZIP is for manual installation and includes a SHA-256 checksum. Stable users remain on v0.5.1; this prerelease is not marked Latest.
